A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEt3R metric and MV-LDM model. Their text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative evaluations on RealEstate10K, along with feature, resolution, sampling, and overlap-mask analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds GSO object-generation evaluations and comparisons with optical-flow warping scores, including a frame-separation experiment.

M1.justification: The DUSt3R reconstruction, DINO/FeatUp features, projection, overlap normalization, and symmetric similarity metric are retained. MV-LDM's architecture, loss, and anchored sampling also match after consulting both appendices; v2's per-block attention description was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond RealEstate10K scene/video generation to object-level generation on Google Scanned Objects. Sections 5.1 and 5.3.3 introduce single-image-conditioned, 360-degree object sequences with loop closure, supported by Figure 7 and Figures 22–25. Existing scene/video coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds RAFT-based flow-warping comparisons using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and RMSE, substantially expanding the pose-free alternatives evaluated against MEt3R. These differ from v1's existing DUSt3R-projection RGB ablations. It also newly evaluates EpiDiff, SyncDreamer, and VideoMV in the object comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 30-object protocol with 16 views at 256x256 resolution, uniformly subsampling VideoMV's 32 outputs, and compares frame gaps of 1 and 10. Table 1 replaces KID with FWS (PSNR). Section 4 changes the reported training budget from 2M to 1.65M iterations, matching v1's appendix; this does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 14 tests how increasing frame separation affects MEt3R and four flow-warping variants, adding a focused robustness analysis. The feature/backbone, training-duration, sampling, and overlap-mask analyses remain. The resolution study moves to Appendix A.2 and receives revised numerical results.

E5.justification: Both versions already report averages across sequences and standard-deviation bands or error bars. v2 introduces no new repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure; additional samples and result rows do not change that practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds GSO results, flow-warping scores in Table 3, and frame-gap comparisons. Figure 7 ranks SyncDreamer ahead of VideoMV and EpiDiff. In retained Table 1, I2VGen-XL's MEt3R changes from 0.051 to 0.050 and SVD's from 0.033 to 0.032; KID entries disappear. Table 2 changes numerous signed differences, including GenWarp's SED difference at 224x224 from +74.70% to -74.84%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content, including the metric definition, feature normalization, diffusion loss, focal-length calculation, and overlap mask. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's claim to the first pose-free consistency metric and Section 5.3.2's corresponding first-metric claim for generated videos. It expands the evaluation contribution to objects while retaining the central MEt3R properties and MV-LDM quality-versus-consistency claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of flow-warping scores' sensitivity to blur, noise, and pixel perturbations, and of LPIPS-based warping failures at larger frame separations. It also interprets object-generation consistency through conditioning strength. The established geometric-prior and image-quality interpretations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies technical information for the added evaluations, including RAFT warping and uniform 32-to-16-view subsampling for VideoMV. It reconciles the main-text training count with the existing appendix. Core hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, and code/model availability statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GSO, EpiDiff, RAFT, and VideoMV and positions MEt3R against existing flow-warping scores while narrowing its novelty claim. SyncDreamer was already cited in v1. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits introduction and experiment prose, shortens baseline descriptions, adds an object-evaluation subsection and a flow-warping appendix section, and relocates the resolution discussion. The abstract, main section sequence, and substantial portions of the method and appendix exposition remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands from four to five metric panels, Table 1 replaces its KID column, and v2 adds the GSO plot, flow-warping table, frame-gap comparison grid, and four object-example figures. Existing diagrams and ablation displays are relocated or reformatted; v1's five scene/video example figures are retained as Figures 17–21.

improvement.justification: The added pose-free flow-warping comparisons, wider-frame-gap test, and GSO evaluation strengthen the empirical justification for MEt3R, while the narrowed novelty claim improves positioning. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: revised Table 2 contains substantial SED decreases while its discussion still describes an increase, and Table 1's new caption calls DFM's FID low despite its worst value. Overall, the expanded validation provides a supported but qualified improvement.
